summary: Your first night in the party's room: At your first {party} meeting, {party official} and {old hand} size you up.
realLife: Around 1880, out of Harvard, he joined his district's Republican association, which met in a room over a saloon. His well-off friends laughed; he kept going, and his first ally was Joe Murray, who knew the district.
gates: You are registered with or lean to {party}.
A local {party} meeting is on the calendar.
weights: Household money: a well-off home makes a scoff at home likelier.
choices: sit in the back and listen
ask {old hand} how things work here

branches.then: Before you go, a parent says these are not your kind of people. Answering that you mean to help run things goes on your record as a stance.
The scoff runs the other way: a relative says those people do not want anyone like you.
After several meetings {old hand} asks you for coffee, the tie a later nomination reads.
